title: Artificial Aeration and Effluent Recirculation to Enhance Nitrogen Removal in Hybrid Constructed Wetland System for Swine Wastewater Treatment
content:
Artificial aeration and 400% effluent recirculation within a VFCW–VFCW–HFCW system increased oxygen availability and promoted sequential nitrification–denitrification. This integrated configuration achieved 90.8% NH4 +-N and 87.2% total nitrogen removal from anaerobically digested swine wastewater, enabling compliance with the applicable nitrogen discharge limit.


ABSTRACT

Constructed wetlands act as self-sufficient and decentralized wastewater treatment systems that are highly effective at filtering pollutants. However, single-stage systems often struggle to meet stringent discharge standards or achieve advanced nutrient removal. Integrating artificial aeration and effluent recirculation into a hybrid constructed wetland (HCW) system was implemented to enhance nitrogen removal in the treatment of anaerobically digested swine wastewater in an on-site experiment lasting 12 months. Two integrated HCW systems were set up, each consisting of a three-stage HCW system, an aeration tower, and a recirculation pump operating at recirculation ratios (RRs) of 400% and 200%, respectively. A conventional three-stage HCW system was also deployed for comparison. The results showed that the removal efficiencies of biological oxygen demand (BOD₅), chemical oxygen demand (COD), ammonia nitrogen (NH₄+-N), and total nitrogen (TN) were significantly improved by artificial aeration as well as effluent recirculation. The highest removal efficiencies were achieved at an RR of 400%, reaching 94.1%, 88.7%, 90.8%, and 87.2%, respectively. Furthermore, the effluent wastewater quality was completely compliant with Vietnamese regulation limits for BOD₅, COD, and TN (no specific limit for NH₄+-N). The nitrogen removal rate at this RR was 0.49 g NH4 +-N/m2.day and 0.84 g TN/m2.day. The VFCW–VFCW–HFCW arrangement was highly suitable, which helped enhance NH₄+-N and TN removal efficiency by facilitating nitrification and denitrification processes.
